root.description: What a document element is about. Hierarchical and single-label: the family is the kind of document, given by its document type, and the leaf is the part of that document the element belongs to, or other.

nodes.label: Annual report
nodes.description: Elements of a company's periodic reports to shareholders and of its proxy statements, whose topics are the parts of such a report, from the shareholder letter and management's discussion to the financial statements and governance. Document types: Annual report, Quarterly report, Proxy statement.

children.label: Shareholder letter
children.description: A narrative letter from the chairman or CEO to shareholders that reviews the year and outlook, as opposed to the formal Business or MD&A sections.
examples: Letter from the Chief Executive Officer

children.label: Business overview
children.description: A description of what the company does, its products, markets, competition, customers, and strategy (Form 10-K Item 1).

children.label: Risk factors
children.description: A discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could materially harm the business or the value of its securities (Item 1A).

children.label: Management discussion and analysis
children.description: Management's narrative explanation of results of operations, liquidity, capital resources, and trends, including market-risk disclosures (MD&A, Items 7 and 7A).
examples: Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

children.label: Financial statements
children.description: The primary statements themselves (balance sheet, income statement, cash flows, changes in equity) and the auditor's report on them, not the accompanying notes.
examples: Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm

children.label: Notes to financial statements
children.description: The numbered explanatory notes on accounting policies, estimates, and line-item detail that accompany and support the financial statements.
examples: Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies

children.label: Corporate governance
children.description: Information about the board of directors, its committees, director independence, officers, and governance practices and policies.
examples: Item 10. Directors, Executive Officers and Corporate Governance

children.label: Executive compensation
children.description: Disclosure of pay for senior executives and directors, including salary, bonuses, equity awards, and pay-versus-performance tables.

children.label: Controls and procedures
children.description: Management's evaluation of disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting, including any material weaknesses (Item 9A).
examples: Management's Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting
Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting

children.label: Legal proceedings
children.description: A description of pending or threatened litigation, regulatory actions, and other legal matters involving the company (Item 3).

children.label: Properties
children.description: A description of the company's principal physical facilities, such as plants, offices, and real estate it owns or leases (Item 2).

children.label: Market for equity
children.description: Information on the market for the company's common stock, including listing, holders, dividends, share repurchases, and stock performance (Item 5).
examples: Item 5. Market for Registrant's Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities

children.label: Exhibits
children.description: The list of exhibits and filed documents, signatures, and schedules incorporated by reference, which carries no narrative content of its own (Item 15).
examples: Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules

children.label: Sustainability
children.description: Material on environmental and social topics such as climate commitments, emissions, workforce, and community impact; it excludes board and corporate governance, which belongs to corporate_governance.

children.label: Other
children.description: Content that fits none of the other categories, such as cover pages, tables of contents, forward-looking-statement legends, and miscellaneous disclosures.

nodes.label: Fund document
nodes.description: Elements of fund and securities-offering documents such as prospectuses and fact sheets, whose topics are the parts of a fund disclosure, from the investment objective and fees to performance and holdings. Document types: Prospectus, Fact sheet.

children.label: Investment objective
children.description: The fund's stated investment goal, such as long-term capital growth, current income, or tracking an index, usually in one or two sentences; how the fund pursues that goal belongs to principal_investment_strategies.

children.label: Fees and expenses
children.description: The costs of buying, holding, and selling fund shares: shareholder fees and sales charges, annual operating expenses and expense ratios, fee waivers, the expense example, and portfolio turnover.
examples: Fees and Expenses of the Fund

children.label: Principal investment strategies
children.description: How the fund pursues its objective: the kinds of securities it buys, its selection process or index methodology, and limits on what it may hold; not the risks of those investments (principal_risks) or the portfolio held on a given date (holdings_and_allocation).
examples: Principal Investment Strategies of the Fund

children.label: Principal risks
children.description: The main risks of investing in the fund or in the offered securities and how they could cause an investor to lose money, such as market, credit, interest-rate, liquidity, and issuer risks; not the strategy that gives rise to them (principal_investment_strategies).
examples: Principal Risks of Investing in the Fund

children.label: Performance
children.description: Past returns of the fund or share class and its benchmark: annual return bar charts, average annual total return tables, best and worst quarters, the growth of a hypothetical investment, and commentary on past results; not the fund's costs (fees_and_expenses).

children.label: Holdings and allocation
children.description: What the fund holds as of a date: its top or full holdings, the number of holdings, and breakdowns by asset class, sector, region, credit quality, or maturity; not the strategy that selects them (principal_investment_strategies).

children.label: Management
children.description: Who runs the fund: the investment adviser and any sub-advisers, the portfolio managers with their tenure and experience, and the management company; the fees paid to them belong to fees_and_expenses.

children.label: Purchase and sale
children.description: How investors buy, sell, exchange, or redeem shares: minimum investments, available share classes, how orders are placed and priced, and exchange trading; the charges on those transactions belong to fees_and_expenses.
examples: Purchase and Sale of Fund Shares

children.label: Tax information
children.description: How the fund's distributions and the sale of its shares are taxed, together with its dividend and capital gain distribution policy; distribution rates and yields as measures of return belong to performance.

children.label: Other
children.description: Content that fits none of the other categories, such as cover pages, tables of contents, fund identifiers from a key-facts block (tickers, inception date, net assets), glossaries, payments to financial intermediaries, service providers, and legal notices; a key-facts block's expense ratio belongs to fees_and_expenses and its number of holdings to holdings_and_allocation.
examples: Payments to Broker-Dealers and Other Financial Intermediaries

nodes.label: Contract
nodes.description: Elements of a legally binding agreement between named parties, whose topics are its clauses, from the parties and recitals to the signatures and exhibits. Document types: Contract.

children.label: Parties and recitals
children.description: The preamble that names the contracting parties, the effective date, and the background recitals (the whereas clauses) that explain the purpose.

children.label: Definitions
children.description: Clauses that define capitalized terms and rules of interpretation used throughout the agreement.

children.label: Scope and services
children.description: The clauses describing the work, services, products, or deliverables that a party is to provide and the standards for providing them.

children.label: Term
children.description: The clauses fixing the duration of the agreement, its effective period, and renewal or extension mechanics.

children.label: Payment
children.description: The clauses on fees, prices, invoicing, payment timing, expenses, taxes, and late-payment consequences.

children.label: Confidentiality
children.description: The clauses obliging the parties to protect each other's non-public information and limiting its use and disclosure.

children.label: Intellectual property
children.description: The clauses on ownership and assignment of, and licenses to, intellectual property such as inventions, work product, trademarks, and software.

children.label: Warranties
children.description: The clauses in which parties represent facts and promise quality or performance standards, together with disclaimers of other warranties.

children.label: Indemnification
children.description: The clauses requiring one party to compensate the other for specified third-party claims, losses, or damages.

children.label: Limitation of liability
children.description: The clauses capping or excluding damages and defining which types of loss each party cannot recover.

children.label: Termination
children.description: The clauses stating how and when either party may end the agreement early, for cause or convenience, and what happens afterwards.

children.label: Governing law and disputes
children.description: The clauses selecting the governing law, jurisdiction or venue, and dispute-resolution method such as arbitration or mediation.

children.label: General provisions
children.description: Boilerplate clauses such as notices, assignment, amendment, severability, entire agreement, force majeure, and counterparts.

children.label: Signatures and exhibits
children.description: The signature blocks and the attached schedules, exhibits, or annexes that complete the agreement.

children.label: Other
children.description: Content of a contract that fits none of the other categories, such as the cover page, table of contents, version or draft markings, and running headers and footers.

nodes.label: Research paper
nodes.description: Elements of a scholarly research paper, whose topics are the parts of a paper, from the abstract and method to the results and references. Document types: Research paper.

children.label: Abstract
children.description: A short self-contained summary of the problem, approach, and main findings placed at the start of the paper.

children.label: Introduction
children.description: The opening section that motivates the problem, states the research questions or contributions, and outlines the paper.

children.label: Related work
children.description: A survey of prior literature that positions the paper against existing approaches.

children.label: Background
children.description: Preliminary definitions, notation, and technical context the reader needs before the method, distinct from the review of competing work.

children.label: Method
children.description: The description of the proposed approach, model, algorithm, or study design, including how data were collected or processed.

children.label: Experiments
children.description: The experimental setup: datasets, baselines, metrics, implementation details, and evaluation protocol, before the numbers are discussed.

children.label: Results
children.description: The reported measurements and findings of the experiments or analyses, presented in tables and figures, without broader interpretation (which belongs to discussion).

children.label: Discussion
children.description: The interpretation of the results: their implications, possible explanations, and comparisons with prior work or expectations, rather than the reported numbers themselves (which belong to results).

children.label: Limitations
children.description: An explicit statement of the weaknesses, assumptions, threats to validity, and scope boundaries of the work.

children.label: Conclusion
children.description: The closing summary of what was shown, with future directions.

children.label: Acknowledgments
children.description: Thanks to funders, colleagues, and reviewers, including funding statements and author contributions.

children.label: References
children.description: The bibliography listing the cited works.

children.label: Appendix
children.description: Supplementary material placed after the main body, such as extra proofs, tables, derivations, and additional experiments.

children.label: Other
children.description: Content of a research paper that fits none of the other categories, such as the title, author names and affiliations, keywords, correspondence details, and running headers and footers.

nodes.label: Technical document
nodes.description: Elements of product and technical documentation such as user manuals and datasheets, whose topics range from installation and configuration to specifications and troubleshooting. Document types: User manual, Datasheet.

children.label: Overview
children.description: A high-level introduction to what the product or system is, its features, purpose, and intended audience.

children.label: Installation and getting started
children.description: Instructions for installing, setting up, or first running the product, including requirements and quick-start steps.

children.label: Configuration
children.description: Explanation of settings, options, parameters, and environment needed to tailor the product's behavior.

children.label: Usage
children.description: Task-oriented instructions and examples showing how to operate the product in normal use.

children.label: Reference
children.description: Lookup material such as API, command, register, message, or function descriptions, organized for consultation rather than reading in order.

children.label: Specifications
children.description: Quantitative technical data such as electrical characteristics, ratings, dimensions, timing, and performance limits, typically in tables.

children.label: Troubleshooting
children.description: Guidance on diagnosing problems, including error messages, symptoms, causes, fixes, and frequently asked questions.

children.label: Appendix
children.description: Supplementary material placed after the main body, such as glossaries, revision history, ordering information, legal notices, and extra tables, as opposed to the lookup material in reference.

children.label: Other
children.description: Content of a technical document that fits none of the other categories, such as cover pages, tables of contents, safety warnings, contact details, and running headers and footers.

nodes.label: Generic document
nodes.description: Elements of any other kind of document, whose topics are the structural parts of a document: front matter, summary, introduction, body, conclusion, references, and appendix. Document types: Shareholder letter, Earnings release, Terms and policies, Court opinion, Legislation, Technical standard, White paper, Government report, Sustainability report, Investor presentation.

children.label: Front matter
children.description: Material that precedes the main content, such as title page, table of contents, preface, copyright notices, and list of figures.

children.label: Summary
children.description: A condensed statement of the key points or findings, such as an executive summary or abstract.

children.label: Introduction
children.description: The opening section that states the purpose, context, and scope of the document.

children.label: Body
children.description: The substantive main content of the document that is neither introductory, concluding, nor back matter.

children.label: Conclusion
children.description: The closing section that wraps up the document with conclusions, recommendations, or next steps.

children.label: References
children.description: Bibliography, citations, footnotes, and links to sources used by the document.

children.label: Appendix
children.description: Supplementary material placed after the main body, such as extra data, tables, forms, and glossaries.

children.label: Other
children.description: Content that is not part of the document's substance and fits none of the other categories, such as distribution lists, document-control blocks, standalone disclaimers, contact details, and running headers and footers.
